definition: a preparation that trains the body to resist a particular disease
modernAnchor: A small jab in the arm that keeps a deadly disease away. We call it a vaccine.
journey: Latin vacca meant cow, and vaccinus meant of or from cows.
In 1796, Edward Jenner noticed that milkmaids who caught cowpox seemed safe from smallpox.
He used cowpox matter to protect a boy, and the method became known as vaccination.
Louis Pasteur later stretched the word to cover every protective shot, whatever animal it came from.
